findings.summary: The corpus schema-conformance tests validate test-local literal objects rather than the corpus runGenerate actually assembles, so they have no power over engine assembly: reverting terminal_marker to a rendered string, or adding a key that violates additionalProperties:false, would not fail either case. The real guard for the fixed blocker is the TypeScript declaration (SynthesizerCorpus.terminal_marker: ReportMarker plus excess-property checking on the annotated literal at src/generate.ts:400-405) enforced by npm run typecheck, not by vitest. Capturing the corpus handed to spawnRole and validating that object would close the gap.

spawnGenerateRole unlinks the --input payload in a finally block. On the success path this runs only after readBody resolves (so the worker has already produced output and read the file), but on a readBody rejection or timeout the payload is deleted while the child may still be alive, reproducing the ENOENT-on---input CONTRACT_ERROR class that src/tick-run.ts:731-741 explicitly bound to onExit rather than finally for exactly this reason.

Both agent-runtime-backed groups (D3 role/route verification and corpus schema conformance) are wrapped in describe.skipIf(!agentRuntimeAvailable), so on any host without the profiles directory and without AGENT_RUNTIME_PROFILES set these gates silently disappear instead of failing loudly. The values themselves are correct — I read profiles/roles/dr-debater-{advocate,opponent,judge}.yaml, dr-synthesizer.yaml and routes.yaml directly — but the gate's presence is environment-dependent.

Dev-note headline count is stale and contradicts its own evidence rows: line 13 claims 317 tests / 12 added, while the D7 row and the verification-commands section both report 319. The 319 figure is the self-consistent one (baseline generate.test.ts had 20 cases, the file now has 34, 305-20+34=319).
